exceptionMessage: The vSAN cache might not be sized correctly
exceptionDetails: This indicates that the read performance might be limited by the size of the vSAN caching tier. This applies to the hybrid vSAN cluster only. In a hybrid vSAN cluster, the read cache stores the data read from the hard disks, so that future reads do not get affected by the hard disk latency. The performance data and graphs listed below include the following metrics to indicate if read cache is not performing optimally: i) rcHitRate, ii) quotaEvictions, and iii) warEvictions. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: vSAN is experiencing congestion in one or more disk group(s)
exceptionDetails: This implies that one or more disk groups are experiencing congestion. The disk group(s) which are experiencing congestion are listed, along with the type of congestion. Note that regardless of the type of congestion, temporary values of congestion are usually ok, and not detrimental to the clusters' performance. However, consistent values of congestion warrant attention and resolution. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: One or more disk group(s) are not in active use
exceptionDetails: This implies that the specified disk groups do not have IOs during some period of the evaluated time duration, which limits the maximum possible performance on the vSAN cluster. The performance data and graphs below show the disk groups and IOs per second. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: One or more disk(s) are not in active use
exceptionDetails: This is applicable to all-flash vSAN clusters only. This implies that one or more disks do not have any IOs. While some disks may not have IOs for some intervals of time, the best performance is usually achieved when IOs are spread across all vSAN capacity devices evenly. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: The outstanding IOs for the benchmark is too high to achieve the desired goal
exceptionDetails: This implies that the outstanding IOs are too high for the desired goal. The outstanding IOs must be low (ideally 1 per host) for minimum latency, or the IOs may queue at different layers leading to higher latency. The remedy is to adjust the outstanding IOs according to the desired goal of performance evaluation. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on how to set the correct outstanding IO.

exceptionMessage: The outstanding IOs for the benchmark is too low to achieve the desired goal
exceptionDetails: This implies that the outstanding IOs are too low for the desired goal. The outstanding IOs must be high (ideally, at least 4 write IOs per host and/or 8 read IOs per host) for maximum IOs per second and maximum throughput, otherwise the system is bottlenecked by the time it takes to process IOs. The remedy is to increase the outstanding IOs. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on how to set the correct outstanding IO.

exceptionMessage: The increase in IO latency in the vSAN stack might be beyond expected limits
exceptionDetails: This implies that the latency seen at the Virtual Machine is much higher than the latency seen in the vSAN capacity devices. The latencies at both layers are reported for each host in the cluster. Write and read latencies are separated. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: The size of IOs is too small to achieve the desired goal
exceptionDetails: The cluster wide throughput and IOs per second are reported from which the average IO size is derived. The IO size must be large (ideally 256K) for the goal of maximum throughput. If your benchmark supports changing the size of IOs that are issued, the remedy is to increase the IO size to get better throughput. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: The size of IOs is too large to achieve the desired goal
exceptionDetails: The cluster wide throughput and IOs per second are reported from which the average IO size is derived. The IO size must be small (ideally 4K) for the goals of maximum IOPs and minimum latency. If your benchmark supports changing the size of IOs that are issued, the remedy is to reduce the IO size. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: Too many IOs are handled by a vSCSI adapter
exceptionDetails: This implies that a single vSCSI adapter is handling much more IOPS than that desired for the best performance. VMware recommends to use a PVSCSI adapter be used for the best performance. For the best performance, each VM can have a maximum of 4 vSCSI adapters. It is recommended that the virtual disks (VMDKs) be distributed evenly across the 4 vSCSI adapters.

exceptionMessage: No benchmark seems to have run during the selected time period
exceptionDetails: No benchmark seems to have run on the vSAN cluster during the selected time period because the read and write IOs per second were below normal threshold.

exceptionMessage: There are losses seen in the TCP layer at one or more hosts
exceptionDetails: vSAN encounters higher transaction latency when out of order packets and retransmissions are seen in the TCP stack. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: There are errors seen in one or more physical NICs on one or more hosts
exceptionDetails: The physical network interface in one or more hosts is dropping packets while transmitting or receiving packets. This could lead to higher latency. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: There are losses seen in one or more virtual NICs on one or more hosts
exceptionDetails: The virtual network interface in one or more hosts is dropping packets while transmitting or receiving packets. This could lead to higher latency. Consult Ask VMware for a recommendation on possible solutions.

exceptionMessage: IO size is too large in HCIBench
exceptionDetails: IO size is too large in HCIBench. Reduce the IO size for better performance.

exceptionMessage: IO size is too small in HCIBench
exceptionDetails: IO size is too small in HCIBench. Increase the IO size for better performance.

exceptionMessage: Too many HCIBench threads per disk
exceptionDetails: Too many HCIBench threads per disk. Reduce the number of threads per disk for better performance.

exceptionMessage: Too many disks in HCIBench
exceptionDetails: Too many disks in HCIBench. Reduce the number of disks for better performance.

exceptionMessage: Too few disks in HCIBench
exceptionDetails: Too few disks in HCIBench. Increase the number of disks for better performance.

exceptionMessage: Too few HCIBench parallel threads per disk
exceptionDetails: Too few HCIBench parallel threads per disk. Increase the number of threads per disk for better performance.
